title: Adding and Subtracting Decimal Fractions
seo_title: Grade 6 Adding and Subtracting Decimals Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Add and subtract decimal fractions with at least 2 decimal places; solve problems in context involving decimal fractions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 worksheets: adding and subtracting decimals, lining up the decimal comma, estimating and decimal problems. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Write the numbers in columns with the decimal commas lined up.
  • Fill empty places with 0: 7,4 − 2,35 → 7,40 − 2,35.
  • Add or subtract as with whole numbers, and put the comma in the answer under the other commas.
  • Estimate first: 7,4 − 2,35 is about 7 − 2 = 5.

Examples

Example

12,6 + 3,85

12,60 + 3,85

Answer: 16,45

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Lining up the last digitsLine up the commas.
An empty placeWrite 0 in it.
The comma movesKeep it under the other commas.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about adding decimals?
faq.a: Add and subtract decimal fractions with at least 2 decimal places.
It makes the columns the same length; the value is the same.

items.q: In 26,38 − 4,51, the digits are lined up by place value. Which digit of 26,38 is above the 4?
items.e: 4 is the ones digit of 4,51. The ones digit of 26,38 is 6, so the 4 goes under the 6. The 2 is in the tens place and has no digit under it.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 5 + 2 = 7. Ones: 7 + 6 = 13, write 13. Answer: 13,7. Check: 13,7 − 6,2 = 7,5.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 5 + 4 = 9. Tenths: 2 + 2 = 4. Ones: 9 + 2 = 11, write 11. Answer: 11,49. Check: 11,49 − 2,24 = 9,25.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 2 + 4 = 6. Ones: 4 + 7 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 6 + 1 = 7. Answer: 71,6. Check: 71,6 − 67,4 = 4,2.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 8 − 7 = 1. Tenths: 4 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 14 − 8 = 6. Ones: 6 − 1 = 5. Answer: 5,61. Check: 5,61 + 1,87 = 7,48.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 2 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 12 − 8 = 4. Ones: 8 − 8 = 0. Tens: bring down 4. Answer: 40,4. Check: 40,4 + 8,8 = 49,2.

items.q: What is 1,9 + 7,8?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 9 + 8 = 17, write 7 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 1 + 7 + 1 = 9. Answer: 9,7. Check: 9,7 − 7,8 = 1,9.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 9 + 4 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 4 + 5 + 1 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 6 + 3 + 1 = 10, write 10. Answer: 10,03. Check: 10,03 − 3,54 = 6,49.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 9 + 9 = 18, write 8 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 6 + 3 + 1 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 8 + 3 + 1 = 12, write 12. Answer: 12,08. Check: 12,08 − 3,39 = 8,69.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 12 − 5 = 7. Tenths: 6 − 6 = 0. Ones: 9 − 3 = 6. Answer: 6,07. Check: 6,07 + 3,65 = 9,72.

items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 2 + 1 = 3. Ones: 2 + 6 = 8. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 18,3. Check: 18,3 − 6,1 = 12,2.

items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 9 + 7 = 16, write 6 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 4 + 7 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. Answer: 9,26. Check: 9,26 − 3,77 = 5,49.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 5 + 1 = 6. Tenths: 1 + 9 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 8 + 8 + 1 = 17, write 17. Answer: 17,06. Check: 17,06 − 8,91 = 8,15.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 1 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 11 − 5 = 6. Tenths: 7 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 17 − 8 = 9. Ones: 2 − 2 = 0. Answer: 0,96. Check: 0,96 + 2,85 = 3,81.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 6 − 4 = 2. Tenths: 5 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 15 − 6 = 9. Ones: 5 − 5 = 0. Tens: bring down 4. Answer: 40,92. Check: 40,92 + 5,64 = 46,56.

items.q: To add 4,5 + 2,37, you write 4,5 with two decimal places. Which number is equal to 4,5?
items.e: A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 4,5 = 4 ones and 5 tenths = 4,50. 4,05 is wrong: it moves the 5 to the hundredths place.

items.q: Sarah lined up the last digits and got 2,82. What is the correct sum?
items.e: Line up the decimal points, not the last digits: 4,50 + 2,37. Hundredths: 0 + 7 = 7. Tenths: 5 + 3 = 8. Ones: 4 + 2 = 6. Answer: 6,87. Estimate: 5 + 2 = 7, so 2,82 is far too small.

items.q: To find 12 + 3,48, you can write 12 with a decimal point. Which number is equal to 12?
items.e: A whole number has its decimal point after the ones digit, so 12 = 12,00. Then the 2 ones sit over the 3 ones: 12,00 + 3,48 = 15,48.

items.q: Kabelo lined up the last digits and got 2,53. What is the correct sum?

Line up the decimal points. Write 0,6 as 0,600. Thousandths: 0 + 5 = 5. Hundredths: 0 + 7 = 7. Tenths: 6 + 2 = 8. Answer: 0,875. Check: 0,875 − 0,275 = 0,6.

items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 4,6 as 4,600. Thousandths: 5 + 0 = 5. Hundredths: 2 + 0 = 2. Tenths: 1 + 6 = 7. Ones: 3 + 4 = 7. Answer: 7,725. Check: 7,725 − 4,6 = 3,125.

items.q: What is 9,84 − 4,9?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 4,9 as 4,90. Hundredths: 4 − 0 = 4. Tenths: 8 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 18 − 9 = 9. Ones: 8 − 4 = 4. Answer: 4,94. Check: 4,94 + 4,9 = 9,84.

items.q: To find 10 − 3,46, how should you write 10 so both numbers have hundredths?
items.e: 10 is 1 ten and 0 ones, and its decimal point is after the 0. Write 10,00: two zeros hold the tenths and hundredths places. Then 10,00 − 3,46 = 6,54.

items.q: Musa found 10 − 3,46 = 6,54. Which addition checks his answer?
items.e: Addition undoes subtraction. Add the answer to the number taken away: 6,54 + 3,46 = 10,00 = 10. You get back the starting number, so his answer is right.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 10 as 10,00. Hundredths: 0 − 6 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 6 = 4. Tenths: 9 − 4 = 5. Ones: 9 − 3 = 6. Answer: 6,54. Check: 6,54 + 3,46 = 10.

items.q: What is 5 − 2,37?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 5 as 5,00. Hundredths: 0 − 7 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 4, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 7 = 3. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 2,63. Check: 2,63 + 2,37 = 5.

items.q: Subtract.

items.q: In the long jump, Johan jumped 3,4 m. His second jump was 0,25 m longer. How long was the second jump?
items.e: Longer means more: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 3,4 as 3,40. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 + 2 = 6. Ones: 3 + 0 = 3. Answer: 3,65. Check: 3,65 − 0,25 = 3,4.

items.q: A bottle holds 1,5 ℓ of water. Ofentse drinks 0,35 ℓ at break. How much water is left?
items.e: Take away what she drank: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 1,5 as 1,50. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 − 3 = 1. Ones: bring down 1. Answer: 1,15. Check: 1,15 + 0,35 = 1,5.

items.q: A ribbon is 2 m long. The class cuts off 0,85 m for a banner. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Take the part cut off away: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 2 as 2,00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 8 = 1. Ones: bring down 1. Answer: 1,15. Check: 1,15 + 0,85 = 2.

items.q: Lethabo's puppy had a mass of 4,6 kg. In a month it gained 0,85 kg. What is its mass now?
items.e: The puppy got heavier: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 4,6 as 4,60. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 4 + 0 + 1 = 5. Answer: 5,45. Check: 5,45 − 0,85 = 4,6.

items.q: In a relay at the swimming gala, Mpho swam the first leg in 32,48 seconds and Lindiwe swam the second leg in 29,75 seconds. What was their total time?
items.e: Total time means add the two legs. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 4 + 7 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 9 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 62,23. Check: 62,23 − 29,75 = 32,48.

items.q: On a road trip, a family drove 125,6 km before lunch and 87,45 km after lunch. How far did they drive altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Line up the decimal points. Write 125,6 as 125,60. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 4 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 5 + 7 + 1 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 2 + 8 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 213,05. Check: 213,05 − 87,45 = 125,6.

items.q: A watermelon has a mass of 3,2 kg. Lungile cuts off a piece with a mass of 1,475 kg. What is the mass of the rest?
items.e: Take away the piece: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 3,2 as 3,200. Thousandths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 tenth: the tenths become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the thousandths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Hundredths: 9 − 7 = 2. Tenths: 1 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 11 − 4 = 7. Ones: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 1,725. Check: 1,725 + 1,475 = 3,2.

items.q: A relay is 3,2 km long. The first runner runs 1,45 km and the second runs 0,9 km. How far does the third runner have to run?
items.e: Step 1, first two runners: 1,45 + 0,9 = 2,35 km. Step 2, the rest: 3,20 − 2,35 = 0,85 km. (1,66 lines up the last digits, 1,45 + 0,9 = 1,54, instead of the decimal points. 2,35 km stops after step 1.)

items.q: At the track and field meet, Tshepo ran the 100 m in 14,62 seconds and Refilwe ran it in 13,87 seconds. How many seconds faster was Refilwe?
items.e: The faster runner has the smaller time. Find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 12 − 7 = 5. Tenths: 5 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 15 − 8 = 7. Ones: 3 − 3 = 0. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 0,75. Check: 0,75 + 13,87 = 14,62.

items.q: At a swim meet, Priya swam 50 m freestyle in 41,36 seconds. Last year her time was 44,08 seconds. By how many seconds did she improve?
items.e: The improvement is the difference between the two times: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 8 − 6 = 2. Tenths: 0 − 3 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 10 − 3 = 7. Ones: 3 − 1 = 2. Tens: 4 − 4 = 0. Answer: 2,72. Check: 2,72 + 41,36 = 44,08.

items.e: Use subtraction: 6 − 2,45 = 6,00 − 2,45 = 3,55. Check: 3,55 + 2,45 = 6,00 = 6. (4,45 forgets to write the zeros: 6 − 2 = 4, then brings down .45. 8,45 adds instead of subtracting.)
